Dev — thanks for the context. High-level guidance below, plus a brief redline approach we should share with Ther aHealth: 

1) Transfer mechanism: Accept SCCs + TIA as primary approach. For the UK, we can include a UK Addendum reference in the DPA (one DPA that supports both mechanisms depending on the destination) — that is our recommended approach to avoid duplicate templates. I'll attach a short UK addendum clause to include.

2) 30-day subprocessor notice: We typically accept a 30-day notice for material subprocessors and a 15-day notice for non-material (telemetry/tooling) where prior category-level notice is provided. Proposed compromise language: 

"Company shall notify Customer at least thirty (30) days in advance of engaging any new Subprocessor that will process Customer Personal Data in connection with the Services. For Subprocessors categorized as non-material (support, telemetry, analytics), Company may provide category-level notice and a fifteen (15) day onboarding period unless Customer reasonably objects in writing."

This preserves our operational agility while giving Ther aHealth the visibility they want.

3) Order Form export control warranty: propose a narrow mutual warranty limited to compliance with applicable export laws and a cooperation clause for remedial measures (e.g., temporary suspension of processing if required by law). Avoid broad indemnities tied to export rules. Suggested Order Form snippet: 

"Each party represents and warrants that it will comply with applicable export controls and trade sanctions. The parties will cooperate in good faith to implement any required restrictions or mitigations. Neither party will be liable for compliance actions taken in good faith to satisfy applicable export laws, except to the extent arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Next steps: I'll draft DPA v2 that includes the UK Addendum reference and the subprocessor compromise language. Karthik — please confirm if the Order Form snippet needs additional limitation of liability tie-outs or if the warranty above is fine.

Attaching: proposed_dpa_redline_v2.docx (draft for internal review).

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / team — I reviewed Laura's approach and agree with the 30/15-day carve. A couple of pragmatic notes: 

- Tie the Order Form warranty to the MSA liability cap: we should ensure the export-control warranty in the Order Form is explicitly subject to the MSA limitations (i.e., do not create a standalone uncapped warranty). Proposed addition: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the liability for claims arising from the export controls warranty shall be subject to the limitation of liability set forth in Section X of the MSA."
- Deal ops: please note this customer is asking for a 12-month retention exception in the Order Form for audit logs; confirm whether we can cap retention at 12 months with an option to extend by mutual written agreement. If retention requests are higher, we should consider a negotiated fee or SLA.

If those two tie-outs are acceptable, I'm happy to approve Laura's DPA v2 for external sharing.

—Karthik
Head of Legal Ops
